--- title: "Converting to `shinyreact`" subtitle: "Converting a Shiny app-package to a React client" author: "Martin Frigaard" date: "2026-11-15" categories: [Shiny, React, Packages] image: "image.png" draft: false toc: true toc-depth: 3 toc-title: 'Contents' toc-location: right --- I saw the [Posit's blog post](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-09-30_introducing-shinyreact/) anouncing the `shinyreact` package and was curious what all the excitement was about. I've worked on a few [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) apps, but couldn't really wrap my head around how Shiny + [React](https://react.dev/) R package would work. I recently built a Shiny app-package for browsing [#TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday) datasets: [`ttdviewer`](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/ttdviewer/). I designed the UI so I could pick a dataset title, view the files in List, Summary, and Graphs (from [`inspectdf`](https://alastairrushworth.com/inspectdf/)). I can also download each dataset as a CSV, `parquet`, or in its original format. `ttdviewer` uses `bslib` (`page_sidebar()`, `sidebar()`, and `navset_tab()`). In this post I'll cover converting the UI to [`shinyreact`](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/), the parts of the conversion the documentation doesn't cover, and the few surprises I hit along the way. ## What is `shinyreact`? `shinyreact` moves the UI *out* of R. The server still holds the reactive graph (`input`, `reactive()`, `req()`, and `bindEvent()` all behave as usual), but the page is a React client we write ourselves. The package supplies the plumbing between the two and no UI components. `shinyreact` is pretty new (version 0.1.0), and the documentation calls it a pre-release, so it's not on CRAN: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r") ``` ::: The R side is small. `page_react()` replaces the UI function and serves a `ui.js` (and `ui.css`) from `src_dir`, and `reactive_output()` sends any R value to the client as JSON: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} ls("package:shinyreact") #> [1] "page_bare" "page_react" "page_react_dep" "page_react_html" #> [5] "reactive_output" "send_message" "wire_tap" ``` ::: On the client, the hooks on `window.shinyreact` read and write Shiny values: `useShinyInput()` sets `input[[id]]`, `useShinyOutputValue()` reads a `reactive_output()`, and `ShinyOutput` and `ImageOutput` host classic Shiny outputs inside React. `ShinyModuleProvider` namespaces the hook ids, so Shiny modules still work. The diagram below shows how values move between the two sides: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph Srv["R server"] RO[["reactive_output()"]] RX[["renderPlot()
renderUI()
downloadHandler()"]] end subgraph Cli["React client"] OV("useShinyOutputValue()") SO("ShinyOutput
ImageOutput") SI("useShinyInput()") end subgraph Inp["R server"] IN[/"input$ds_title"/] end RO -->|"i. JSON value"| OV RX -->|"ii. classic output"| SO SI -->|"iii. user choice"| IN style Srv fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style Cli fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style Inp fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style RO fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style RX fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style IN fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style OV fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style SO fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style SI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 ``` ## Spike first The documentation only shows R examples for `plotly` and `reactable`. It doesn't mention `listviewerlite`, `renderPlot()`, `downloadHandler()`, or serving the client from an installed R package. Those are four of the app's five outputs, so before touching the package I built a small prototype (a spike) to test each one with Netflix Titles (one file) and Space Launches (two files). All four worked. ### Lists `listviewerlite::listview()` returns HTML, so the server keeps `renderUI()`, and the client hosts it with the `shiny-html-output` class: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} output$list <- renderUI({ req(data()) listviewerlite::listview(data()) }) ``` ::: ```{.default} ``` ### Plots `ImageOutput` is only documented for Python, but it follows the same contract as R's `renderPlot()`. The client reports its size through `.clientdata_output__width` and `_height`, and draws the image `renderPlot()` sends back. The `inspect_plot()` ggplots rendered unchanged: ```{.default} ``` ### Downloads `downloadHandler()` binds to an anchor with the `shiny-download-link` class, so a `ShinyOutput` with `tagName="a"` works: ```{.default} Download Data ``` The CSV download for Netflix Titles returned 3.0 MB, and the two file zip for Space Launches returned 104 KB. ### Packaging `page_react()` passes `src_dir` to `page_react_dep()`, which builds an `htmltools::htmlDependency()` with a file source. File sources work from an installed package, so the built client belongs in `inst/www/`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} app_ui <- function() { shinyreact::page_react( useBusyIndicators(spinners = TRUE, pulse = TRUE), src_dir = system.file("www", package = "ttdviewer"), theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5), title = "#TidyTuesday Viewer" ) } ``` ::: `bs_theme(version = 5)` keeps Bootstrap on the page, so the React components can use the same classes (`form-select`, `nav-tabs`, `card`) the `bslib` UI used. ## The conversion The conversion lives on its own branch, so `main` keeps the `bslib` app. The spike was built outside the repo, so the branch starts with the full conversion in one commit (`0dbf03e`). The graph below shows how the two branches relate: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'gitGraph': {'mainBranchName': 'main', 'showCommitLabel': true, 'rotateCommitLabel': false}, 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false, 'git0': '#4CBB9D', 'git1': '#E83E8C', 'gitBranchLabel0': '#FFFFFF', 'gitBranchLabel1': '#FFFFFF', 'commitLabelFontSize': '12px'}}}%% gitGraph LR: commit id: "91bc354: zip support, 2026 data" commit id: "d3f3d7b: report and tables" commit id: "ab7a2e3: TidyTuesday date" commit id: "7202318: data vignette" branch shinyreact checkout shinyreact commit id: "0dbf03e: convert UI to shinyreact" type: HIGHLIGHT commit id: "796b3b7: conversion vignette" checkout main commit id: "c03fa33: tab order (bslib)" checkout shinyreact commit id: "5f4a1df: tab order (React)" ``` The branches don't share UI code anymore, so a UI change has to be made twice. Reordering the tabs (Summary, Graphs, List) took one commit on `main` (`R/app_ui.R`) and another on `shinyreact` (`js/src/ui.tsx`, then a rebuilt `inst/www/ui.js`). ### The client The client lives in `js/`, a Vite and TypeScript (TSX) project. `npm run build` writes `inst/www/ui.js` and `ui.css`. React isn't bundled, because `shinyreact.js` (served by the R package) already provides it, so Vite maps `react` to the global `shinyreact.React`: ```{.default} rollupOptions: { external: ["react"], output: { globals: { react: "shinyreact.React" } }, }, ``` `js/` is in `.Rbuildignore`, and the built bundle is committed, so installing the package doesn't require Node. The path from source files to the browser looks like this: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false}}}%% flowchart TD Src[("js/src/
TSX components")] Build[["npm run build
(Vite)"]] WWW[("inst/www/
ui.js + ui.css")] UI[["app_ui()
page_react()"]] Br(["Browser"]) Src -->|"i. compile"| Build Build -->|"ii. write bundle"| WWW WWW -->|"iii. installed with
the package"| UI UI -->|"iv. serve"| Br style Src fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style Build fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style WWW fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style UI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style Br fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 ``` ### The modules Every `mod_*_ui()` function is gone. Each server module keeps its id, and the client wraps the matching component in a `ShinyModuleProvider` with the same namespace: ```{.default} ``` The namespace strings on the client have to match the module ids in `app_server()`: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph Cli["ui.tsx"] CI("TitleInput") CD("Download") CL("ListTab") CS("SummaryTab") CP("GraphsTab") end subgraph Srv["app_server()"] MI[["mod_input_server('input')"]] MD[["mod_download_server('download')"]] ML[["mod_list_server('listviewerlite')"]] MS[["mod_summary_server('summary')"]] MP[["mod_plot_server('viz')"]] end CI <-.->|"input"| MI CD <-.->|"download"| MD CL <-.->|"listviewerlite"| ML CS <-.->|"summary"| MS CP <-.->|"viz"| MP style Srv fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style Cli fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style MI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style MD fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style ML fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style MS fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style MP fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style CI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CD fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CL fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CS fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CP fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 ``` Plain values (the dataset titles, file names, and the Summary file overview) moved to `reactive_output()`. For example, `mod_input_server()` used to get its choices from `selectInput()` in the UI module. Now it sends them: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} output$titles <- shinyreact::reactive_output( unique(all_tt_combined$title) ) ``` ::: And `TitleInput.tsx` reads the titles and sends the selection back as `input$ds_title`: ```{.default} const titles = asArray(useShinyOutputValue("titles", [])); const [title, setTitle] = useShinyInput("ds_title", "Space Launches"); ``` The table below maps each module to its outputs and client component: | Module | R output | Client | |---|---|---| | `mod_input` | `titles` (`reactive_output()`) | `TitleInput.tsx` | | `mod_download` | `download` (`downloadHandler()`) | `Download.tsx` | | `mod_list` | `list` (`renderUI()`) | `ListTab.tsx` | | `mod_summary` | `overview`, `choices` (`reactive_output()`); `stats`, `vars`, `table` (`renderReactable()`) | `SummaryTab.tsx` | | `mod_plot` | `datasets` (`reactive_output()`); `plt_` (`renderPlot()`) | `GraphsTab.tsx` | ### `mod_plot_server()` The plot module changed the most. The `bslib` version populated a dataset `selectInput()` with `updateSelectInput()`, created `renderPlot()` calls inside an observer, and built the plot containers with `renderUI()`. It also piped `return(...)` into `bindEvent()`, so the `bindEvent()` never ran. The new version creates one `renderPlot()` per plot type up front, and each one is gated by `req()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} purrr::walk(PLOT_TYPES, function(plt) { output[[paste0("plt_", plt)]] <- renderPlot({ req(plt %in% input$plots) ds <- selected() #<1> tryCatch( inspect_plot(ttd = ds, plots = plt), error = function(err) { plot.new() text(0.5, 0.5, "Error generating plot", cex = 1.2, col = "red") } ) }) }) ``` ::: 1. outside `tryCatch()` so `req()` is not caught as an error The checkboxes and plot containers now live in `GraphsTab.tsx`, and `PLOT_TYPES` has to match in both places. ## Surprises ### Length one vectors `reactive_output()` passes the R value through unchanged, and Shiny serializes it with `auto_unbox`, so a character vector of length one arrives as a string, not an array. The spike's server sent the file names and the TidyTuesday date for the selected title: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} output$files <- reactive_output({ if (is.null(input$title)) return(NULL) d <- data() list(names = names(d), date = format(attr(d[[1]], "date"))) }) ``` ::: And the client joined the names into a single line: ```{.default} files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", files.names.join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date), ``` The spike's default title was Netflix Titles, which has one file. The app crashed on load, and the browser console showed: ```{.default} TypeError: files.names.join is not a function at App (http://localhost:8765/spike-1795198398/ui.js:20:61) at vf (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:47833) at Yf (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:70472) at Gd (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:80765) at ry (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:116187) at Kr (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115267) at uc (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115104) at cy (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:111963) at My (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:123483) at MessagePort.It (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:17:1579) ``` Shiny's internal `toJSON()` shows why. One file arrives as a string, and two files arrive as an array: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # one file (Netflix Titles) shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("netflix_titles.csv"))) #> {"names":"netflix_titles.csv"} # two files (Space Launches) shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("agencies.csv", "launches.csv"))) #> {"names":["agencies.csv","launches.csv"]} ``` ::: The spike fixed the client line with `[].concat()`, which turns a string into a one element array and leaves an array alone: ```{.default} files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", [].concat(files.names).join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date), ``` We can also protect the vector on the server with `I()`, which keeps it an array: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} shiny:::toJSON(list(names = I("netflix_titles.csv"))) #> {"names":["netflix_titles.csv"]} ``` ::: Or we can wrap it on the client, so every `reactive_output()` is covered. In the package, I went with a small client helper: ```{.default} export function asArray(x: T | T[] | null | undefined): T[] { if (x === null || x === undefined) return []; return Array.isArray(x) ? x : [x]; } ``` ### Outputs that never rendered `app_server()` has a `dev` output (a `listview()` of the reactive values) in a closed `
` element in the sidebar. In the `bslib` UI it never rendered. Inside React it does, and `listviewerlite::listview()` errors on `NULL` elements (before a title loads). It now drops them with `purrr::compact()`. ### No type to search The title picker is a native `
